prompt:
Please prepare my final Seattle trip plan from our conversation below. The messages are chronological; a later message replaces only the detail it explicitly changes. Everything else remains in force.

INITIAL REQUEST
Maya and Leo are visiting Seattle from Thursday, October 22 through Sunday, October 25, 2026. We arrive at King Street Station at 09:40 Thursday and leave from the same station at 18:40 Sunday. We are staying all three nights at Pine Street Guesthouse, can leave bags there before check-in and after checkout, and will not have a car. Keep estimated walking to 4 miles or less each day and schedule no more than two anchor activities per day. Our interests are public art, independent bookstores, gardens, and local history. Include a vegetarian meal idea every day, but do not present a restaurant's current menu or dietary accommodation as verified. I have a remote call at the hotel on Friday from 13:00 to 15:00 PT. Use these anchor pairings: Seattle Central Library and Olympic Sculpture Park on Thursday; Pike Place Market and Elliott Bay Book Company on Friday; Seattle Japanese Garden and Frye Art Museum on Saturday; and MOHAI and Lake Union Park on Sunday.

CLARIFICATION
Use a morning/afternoon/evening plan with times and transit or walking notes. On Friday and Saturday, make one anchor primarily indoor and one primarily outdoor. Give every outdoor anchor a named indoor rain fallback from the supplied notes. Keep every evening after 20:00 unscheduled. On Sunday, finish sightseeing by 14:00 and remain at the guesthouse, King Street Station, or in transit between them after that time. Clearly distinguish fixed commitments, anchor activities, meals, and transit.

CORRECTION
Only the remote-call timing has changed: it is Saturday from 10:00 to 12:00 PT at the hotel, not Friday. Friday 13:00 to 15:00 is now available; use that newly open window for Elliott Bay Book Company.

FINAL DELIVERY REQUEST
Create a substantive final plan in `travel_plan.md`; do not merely describe how you would plan it. Use `venue_notes.md` as the factual source and do not claim live availability, reservations, menus, weather, or real-time transit. Start with a constraint summary that shows the retained trip details and corrected call time. Then provide `## Recommended itinerary` with a separate `###` heading for each day. Under each day, use a Markdown table with columns `Time | Type | Plan | Travel / mobility | Why it fits`; use `Anchor`, `Fixed`, `Meal`, or `Transit` in the Type column. Include exactly two Anchor rows per day, a `Transit plan:` line, an `Estimated walking: N.N miles` line, a `Vegetarian meal idea:` line, a `Rain fallback:` line naming an indoor venue from the notes, and an `Evening plan:` line confirming that time after 20:00 is unscheduled. After the itinerary, add separate `## Sourced facts used`, `## Recommendations and rationale`, and `## Uncertainty and checks` sections. In sourced facts, include one row for every scheduled anchor, cite its exact heading from `venue_notes.md`, and report the listed hours or variable-hours note plus any admission or ticket-availability caveat that affects planning. Keep those sourced facts separate from your choices and explain the recommendation rationale. State what remains uncertain and what the travelers should recheck shortly before the trip.
